overview: Emausaurus was a small early armoured dinosaur from northern Germany, known from Toarcian rocks of the Early Jurassic. It sits close to the base of Thyreophora, the lineage that later produced stegosaurs and ankylosaurs, so even fragmentary material is useful for understanding how dinosaur body armour first evolved.

The fossil record is limited, but the animal is important because it is the only formally named dinosaur from its local Toarcian zone and one of the few early Jurassic thyreophorans from Europe. PBDB records it from Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, while Wikipedia notes the Lehmhagen Member as the source unit.

articles.title: Why it matters
articles.body: Emausaurus helps fill the early history of armoured dinosaurs before the spectacular plates of stegosaurs and heavy ankylosaur armour evolved.

articles.title: Evidence limit
articles.body: The genus is based on sparse material, so body size, detailed armour arrangement and ecology should be treated cautiously.

record.description: Emausaurus ernsti was an early armoured ornithischian from the Ciechocinek Formation of northern Germany. It is known from one incomplete, probably immature skeleton with a partial skull and scattered osteoderms; most of the limbs and tail are missing.
facts: The wiki Middle Jurassic age is incorrect; Emausaurus is Early Jurassic.
The specimen is immature and incomplete.
It was a herbivorous thyreophoran, but its complete armour arrangement is unknown.
